definition: Parallel lines go in the same direction and stay the same distance apart, so they never meet; on a grid, parallel lines that are not vertical have equal gradients.
Perpendicular lines meet or cross at a right angle, $90^{\circ}$.
The line that cuts a line segment into two equal halves and crosses it at right angles; every point on it is the same distance from both ends.
A corner of a shape or solid, where sides or edges meet; the plural is vertices.
An angle of exactly $90^{\circ}$, a quarter turn, marked on diagrams with a small square.
An angle between $0^{\circ}$ and $90^{\circ}$.
An angle between $90^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}$.
An angle between $180^{\circ}$ and $360^{\circ}$.
Congruent shapes are exactly the same shape and size, so one fits exactly on the other, even after turning or flipping it.
A triangle with three equal sides and three equal angles of $60^{\circ}$.
A triangle with two equal sides, where the two angles opposite those sides are also equal.
A triangle with no equal sides and no equal angles.
A triangle with one angle of $90^{\circ}$.
A flat shape with four straight sides, whose four angles add up to $360^{\circ}$.
A quadrilateral with two pairs of equal sides, where the two sides in each pair are next to each other.
A quadrilateral with four equal sides, whose opposite sides are parallel and opposite angles are equal.
A quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel sides, whose opposite sides are equal and opposite angles are equal.
A quadrilateral with one pair of parallel sides, where the other two sides are not parallel.
A flat, closed shape with straight sides, such as a pentagon ($5$ sides), hexagon ($6$), octagon ($8$) or decagon ($10$), which is regular if all its sides and angles are equal and irregular if not.
A flat surface that goes on for ever in every direction, such as the surface that a flat face of a solid lies in.
A solid box shape with six rectangular faces.
A solid with flat faces and the same cross-section all the way through, named after that cross-section, such as a triangular prism.
A solid with two equal circular ends joined by a curved surface, like a prism with a circular cross-section.
A solid with a flat base and triangular faces that meet at one vertex at the top.
A solid with a circular base and a curved surface that rises to a point.
A perfectly round solid, like a ball, where every point on the surface is the same distance from the centre.
Half of a sphere, with one flat circular face and one curved surface.
The part of a cone or pyramid that is left when the top is cut off parallel to the base.
One flat surface of a solid; two faces meet at an edge.
The distance from the centre of a circle to any point on the circle, or a line joining them; the plural is radii.
A chord that passes through the centre of a circle, twice as long as the radius.
The whole distance round a circle, or the curve itself.
Half of a circle, cut off by a diameter.
A straight line joining two points on a circle.
A straight line that touches a circle at exactly one point, or, for a curve, the straight line that just touches it at a point and is as steep as the curve there.
Part of the circumference of a circle; between two points, the shorter arc is the minor arc and the longer one is the major arc.
The region of a circle between two radii and the arc joining their ends, like a slice of pizza.
The region of a circle between a chord and an arc.
